**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 83, verse 7:**

His saying, Exalted and Majestic is He: ﴿Nay﴾ is a deterrent (*radʻ*), meaning: the matter is not as they are upon, so let them desist. The complete statement ends here. Al-Hasan said: "*Kalla*" is a new beginning that connects with what follows it, with the meaning of "truly." ﴿Indeed, the record of the wicked﴾, in which their deeds are written, ﴿is in Sijjin﴾. ʻAbdullah ibn ʻUmar, Qatadah, Mujahid and al-Dahhak said: ﴿Sijjin﴾ is the lowest, seventh earth, in which are the spirits of the disbelievers.

Abu Saʻid al-Shurayhi informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Thaʻlabi informed us: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Musa ibn Muhammad related to us: al-Hasan ibn ʻAlawayh related to us: Ismaʻil ibn ʻIsa informed us: al-Musayyib related to us: al-Aʻmash related to us, from al-Minhal, from Zadhan, from al-Bara', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "*Sijjin* is beneath the seven earths, and *ʻIlliyyun* is in the seventh heaven beneath the Throne."[[Narrated by Imam Ahmad at length: 4/287-288, where it includes "...Allah, Exalted and Majestic, says: Write his book in Sijjin, in the lowest earth..." and by al-Tayalisi in his Musnad, p. 102. It is narrated in abridged form by Abu Dawud in the Book of Funerals, chapter "Sitting at the Grave": 4/337, and by al-Nasa'i in the Book of Funerals, chapter "Standing for Funerals": 4/78. Al-Hakim authenticated it at length in al-Mustadrak: 1/37-38 and cited supporting narrations. Ibn al-Qayyim said in Tahdhib al-Sunan (4/337): Abu Hatim ibn Hibban criticized it, saying: Zadhan did not hear it from al-Bara'. This defect is invalid, for Zadhan said: "I heard al-Bara' ibn ʻAzib say" and then mentioned it. Abu ʻAwanah al-Isfara'ini mentioned it in his Sahih. Ibn Hazm criticized it on account of the weakness of al-Minhal ibn ʻAmr. This defect is also invalid, for al-Minhal is trustworthy and truthful. Abu Nuʻaym and others authenticated it.]]

Shamir ibn ʻAtiyyah said: Ibn ʻAbbas came to Kaʻb al-Ahbar and said: "Tell me about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Majestic: ﴿Indeed, the record of the wicked is in Sijjin﴾." He said: "The spirit of the wicked person is raised up to the heaven, but the heaven refuses to accept it. Then it is lowered to the earth, but the earth refuses to accept it, so it enters beneath the seven earths until it reaches Sijjin, which is the place of Iblis's army. From Sijjin a parchment (*raqq*) is brought out for it, which is inscribed and sealed and placed beneath the army of Iblis, because it knows the destruction awaiting it on the Day of Resurrection."[[Narrated by al-Tabari: 30/95. The narrator of al-Tabari's chain has weakness. al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur 8/443 to Ibn al-Mubarak in al-Zuhd, ʻAbd ibn Humayd, and Ibn al-Mundhir.]] This is also the view of Saʻid ibn Jubayr, who said: "Sijjin is beneath the army of Iblis."

ʻAta' al-Khurasani said: It is the lowest earth, and in it are Iblis and his offspring.

al-Kalbi said: It is a rock beneath the lowest, seventh earth, green, and the greenness of the heavens comes from it. The record of the wicked is placed in it.

Ibn Abi Najih related from Mujahid also, who said: "Sijjin" is a rock beneath the lowest earth, which is turned over, and the record of the wicked is placed in it. Wahb said: It is the last domain of Iblis.

It has come in a hadith: "*Al-Falaq* is a well (*jubb*) in Hell, covered over, and *Sijjin* is a container (*habb*) in Hell, open."[[Narrated by al-Tabari: 30/96. The Hafiz Ibn Kathir said (4/486): "It is a strange, munkar hadith that is not sound. The correct view is that Sijjin is derived from *al-sijn*, which means narrowness. Every created thing that is lower is narrower, and every created thing that is higher is wider. The seven spheres are each wider and higher than the one beneath it, and likewise the earths, each wider than the one beneath it, until absolute lowness and the narrowest place end at the center in the middle of the seventh earth. Since the destination of the wicked is Hell, which is the lowest of the low, as Allah says: ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low, except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, and here He says: ﴿Nay, indeed the record of the wicked is in Sijjin. And what can make you know what Sijjin is?﴾, it combines narrowness and lowness."]]

ʻIkrimah said: "﴿in Sijjin﴾" means: in loss and misguidance. Al-Akhfash said: It is *fiʻkīl* from *al-sijn* (imprisonment), as one says *fisseeq* (*fisiq*, "a great transgressor") and *shirreeb* (*shiribb*, "a great drinker"), meaning: in confinement and severe constriction.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 83, verses 8–9:

﴿And what will make you know what Sijjin is?﴾ [Al-Zajjaj said:] [[Omitted from manuscript "A".]] That is, this is not something you or your people knew.

﴿It is a written record.﴾ This is not an explanation of Sijjin; rather, it is an explanation of the record mentioned in His words: "Indeed, the record of the wicked..." That is, it is a written record, meaning that their deeds are written down and recorded against them like a mark in cloth, neither forgotten nor erased, until they are recompensed for it. Qatadah and Muqatil said: it was marked upon with their associates, as if it were marked with a sign by which it is known that he is a disbeliever. It was also said: it is sealed (makhtum), in the dialect of Himyar.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 83, verses 10–15:

﴿Woe that Day to the deniers, who deny the Day of Judgment. None denies it except every transgressor, sinful, who, when Our verses are recited to him, says, "Tales of the ancients." No!﴾ Muqatil said: meaning, they do not believe. Then he resumed and said: ﴿Rather, what they used to earn has rusted over their hearts.﴾

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abd al-Samad al-Turabi informed us; Abu Muhammad Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hamawayh al-Sarakhsi related to us; Ibrahim ibn Hizyam al-Shashi informed us; Abu Muhammad Abd [[In the original: Abd Allah.]] ibn Humayd al-Kashshi informed us; Safwan ibn Isa related to us, from Ibn Ajlan, from al-Qa'qa' ibn Hakim, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the believer commits a sin, a black spot appears on his heart. If he repents, gives it up and seeks forgiveness, his heart is polished of it. But if he increases (in sin), it increases until it covers his heart." That is the "rust" (al-ran) which Allah mentioned in His Book: "No! Rather, what they used to earn has rusted over their hearts." [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in Tafsir, Tafsir of Surah al-Mutaffifin: 9/253–254, and he said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith." Also by al-Nasa'i in Tafsir: 2/505, and in 'Amal al-Yawm wal-Layla, p. 317, no. 418; Ibn Majah in al-Zuhd, Bab Dhikr al-Dhunub, no. 4244, 2/1418; Imam Ahmad: 2/297; al-Tabari: 30/98. al-Hakim authenticated it: 2/517, and al-Dhahabi agreed with him. Ibn Hibban, no. 1771, p. 439; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/89.]]

The root of "al-rayn" is domination. It is said: "wine overcame his intellect (raanat al-khamr 'ala 'aqlihi) and it overpowers (tarin), ran (rayban) and ruyun (ruyunan), when it dominates him so that he becomes intoxicated." The meaning of the verse is: sins dominated their hearts and encompassed them. Al-Hasan said: it is sin upon sin until the heart dies. Ibn Abbas said: "ran 'ala qulubihim" means "sealed upon them."

﴿No! Indeed they, on that Day, from their Lord﴾ (that is, the Day of Resurrection) ﴿will be veiled.﴾ [Ibn Abbas said: "No" means: they will not believe. Then he resumed and said: "Indeed they, on that Day, from their Lord, will be veiled."] [[The text between the brackets is missing from "B".]] Some of them said: they will be kept from His honor and mercy [[In "B": mamnu'un (prevented).]]. Qatadah said: it means that He will not look at them and will not purify them. Most of the exegetes said: they will be kept from seeing Him. al-Hasan said: If the ascetics and worshippers knew that they would not see their Lord in the afterlife, their souls would depart in this world.

al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: Just as He veiled them from His oneness in this world, He veils them from seeing Him in the Hereafter.

Malik was asked about this verse and said: When Allah veiled His enemies so that they did not see Him, He manifested Himself to His friends until they saw Him.

al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, said: In His saying: "No! Indeed they, on that Day, from their Lord, will be veiled" there is evidence that the friends of Allah will see Allah. [[The Hafiz Ibn Kathir said (4/487): "What Imam al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said is in the utmost excellence, and it is an inference from the implication of this verse, just as the explicit statement of His saying, Exalted is He: 'Faces that Day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord' indicates it, and as the sound and mutawatir hadiths indicate concerning the believers seeing their Lord, Mighty and Majestic, in the Hereafter, a vision with the eyes on the plains of resurrection and in the splendid gardens of Paradise."]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 83, verse 27–29:

﴿And its mixture is from Tasnim﴾: It is a drink that pours down upon them from above, in their chambers and their dwellings. It is also said: it flows in the air, raised high, and then pours into the vessels of the people of Paradise according to their measure; when they are filled, it stops. This is the meaning of the statement of Qatadah.

The root of the word tasnim (Tasnim, a spring in Paradise) is from "al-uluw" (height). For anything elevated, the word sanam (hump) is used, and from it comes sanam al-ba'ir (the hump of the camel). Al-Dahhak said: it is a spring whose name is Tasnim, and it is the most noble of drinks.

Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Abbas said: it is pure for the muqarrabun (those brought near), who drink it unmixed, and it is mixed for the rest of the people of Paradise. This is His saying: ﴿from Tasnim, a spring from which those brought near drink﴾.

Yusuf ibn Mihran narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he was asked about His saying "from Tasnim", and he said: this is of what Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes﴾ [al-Sajdah: 17].

﴿A spring﴾ is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal). ﴿from which they drink﴾, i.e., from it. It is also said: those brought near drink it unmixed.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes﴾, i.e., associated partners with Allah, meaning the disbelievers of Quraysh: Abu Jahl, al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, al-'As ibn Wa'il, and their companions from the affluent people of Makkah, ﴿used to laugh at those who believed﴾, i.e., 'Ammar, Khabbab, Suhayb, Bilal, and their companions from the poor believers.

﴿They used to laugh﴾, and mock them.
